Commentary.Commentary: A clinical bowling show by the Aussies but now they have to bat very well on this wicket which already is offering spin. Rangana Herath will be the real danger man. Stay tuned for Australia's reply.

That's the end of Sri Lanka's shockingly brief first innings. With the big five batsmen already dismissed in the first session, the Lankans were simply looking to survive out there. However, the Aussies had other plans and Nathan Lyon got them off to a roaring start in the 2nd Session. He claimed Kusal Perera's scalp and soon followed it up with two more. Stephen O'Keefe removed Nuwan Pradeep to end  a truly disastrous innings for the home side.

OUT! Edged and gone! Extra loopy ball around off, full and spinning away, Pradeep gets forward, tries to defend with a straight bat but it turns away to take the outside edge. Smith gobbles it at first slip and that will be it for the hosts. SRI LANKA BOWLED OUT FOR 117!
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Sandakan is adding useful runs to the board! Starc once again spears in a very full ball on middle and leg, Sandakan hops back and drills it through covers for a boundary.
Starc spears in a full ball again, on middle and leg, Sandakan goes back and drives it to mid off.
Oohhh...misses the off stump not by much! Starc tries to bowl a yorker but only manages to serve a full toss on off, Sandakan swings and misses.
FOUR! Boom! This time Sandakan connects. Starc serves it short and outside off, the debutant makes some room as well and then spanks it through backward point for a boundary.
Full this time, around off at 148 kph, Sandakan somehow keeps it out towards mid off.
Short and wide outside off, Sandakan goes deep inside the crease and tries to cut but fails to connect.
Aahhh...beautiful bowling. Drifting into the batsman, slower in pace, 72 kph, it lands on middle, opens Pradeep in defense and then spins away to beat the bat. It goes over the off stump.
Loopy and around off, Pradeep tries to defend but it spins away a bit to beat the outside edge.
Shortish outside off, tapped to point for a single.
FOUR! Slower loopy ball outside off, Sandakan goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
FOUR! Wow, counter-attack from the debutant. He dances down the track to a full ball and hammers it through mid on for a boundary.
Tossed up ball outside off, Sandakan leaves it alone.
STEPHEN O'KEEFE is back on.
NUWAN PRADEEP is the last batsman.

OUT! IT'S BOOT FIRST! And the decision is overturned. Starc spears in a very full ball around off, 147 kph, Herath is almost beaten by the pace as he brings his bat down to dig it out. The Australians appeal as they feel it's boot first but the umpire thinks it's bat and hence turns down the appeal. Steven Smith opts for the DRS and after watching multiple replays from all the angles, the third umpire decides that it indeed was boot first. Now he takes a look at the Hawk Eye and there is no question where the ball is heading - crashing into middle stump! Herath is out of here.
Appeal for an lbw, it's not entertained by the umpire and Australia have opted for the DRS. Is it boot first or bat?
On a length and outside off, Herath flashes his bat at it but mistimes his shot to the off side.
Around off and shorter in length, Herath goes for the pull but ends up getting an inside edge on his body.
Smart thinking by the bowler, he slips in a 145 kph fullish ball as the follow-up delivery for a shorter one, Herath does well to keep it out towards covers.
FOUR! Short ball on off, jumping onto the batsman, Herath does well to control his pull shot and places it over square leg for a boundary. 100 UP FOR SRI LANKA!
Starc comes from round the wicket and angles in a full ball down the leg side, Sandakan flicks it through square leg for a run.
Flighted ball on off, Sandakan tries to drive it through covers but it comes off the outside half of the bat and rolls wide of backward point. They cross for a run.
Flatter full ball on off, 89 kph, Sandakan defends it off his front foot.
A silly point comes into place now. There is a slip and short leg already in place.
Quicker one down the leg side, Sandakan fails to flick.
Tossed up ball on middle, Sandakan flicks it off his pads to the leg side.
Debutant Lakshan Sandakan walks in next.

OUT! Boom, another wicket down and Lyon is roaring at the moment. He serves a flighted full ball around off, Perera gets a bit forward and then decides to leave it. He thought it will spin away but to his surprise and bad luck, it carries on with the angle and goes on to hit the off pole. Australia are delighted and Sri Lanka are struggling to even cross the 100-run mark.
Full flighted ball on off, Perera pushes it from the crease to covers.
Good length ball down the leg side, Herath tries to work it off his pads but fails to make any connection.
This one is very full and on off, Herath drives it from the crease and finds the gap at covers. They take a couple of runs.
Arrows in a length ball on middle and leg, 144 kph, Herath defends it off his back foot to short leg.
Another sharp delivery, this time it's full and sliding down the leg side, Perera nudges it to fine leg and gets off strike.
FOUR! Starc delivers a sharp short delivery on off, Perera goes on the back foot and glides it down to third man for a boundary.
Fullish and shaping in, Perera keeps it out off the inside half of the bat to mid on.
Gets forward and defends. End of a impressive over!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
RANGANA HERATH is in next.

OUT! Plumb in front and Lyon hunts down another wicket in this over. Australia all over Sri Lanka like a rash. Lyon gives this one flight and lands it full outside, the ball spins in sharply after landing and catches Perera on the pads who is stuck inside the crease. That looked dead plumb to the naked eye and umpire Kettleborough raises his finger to confirm the same. The devil's number strikes twice!
Tossed up ball again on middle, defended off the pads to the leg side.
DILRUWAN PERERA is the new batsman.

OUT! Gone this time! Lyon gets his first wicket. A touch quicker through the air, around middle, 89 kph, de Silva goes back to turn it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It loops in the air then and Burns takes a simple catch at forward short leg. Great start to the session again for Australia! Sri Lanka are 87/6, the devil's number strikes.

EDGED BUT SAFE! Loopy off-spinner on off, fuller in length, Perera gets forward in defense but the ball spins away to catch the outside edge. Smith dives to his left from first slip but it goes wide of him. The fielder chases it down and they take three runs.

We're back. The men concerned are out in the middle. Sri Lanka will be hoping to fight with the remaining wickets while Australia would look to bundle them out in this session. Nathan Lyon to begin proceedings...
DAY 1, SECOND SESSION...

Australia have been excellent. Not because they have picked up 5 wickets but for the way they have got those. Starc got some swing early on, but then that disappeared. Soon, the Aussies started to alter their length, mixing fuller and shorter stuff and the result is that half the Sri Lankan team is back in the dressing room. One good thing is that every bowler has been economical, (not counting Lyon as he has bowled just a solitary over) and that is not helping Sri Lanka. Join us back at 1240 IST (0710 GMT) for the second session.

Right now, this pair of Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Perera are trying to counter-attack again. That could go both ways, as seen with Chandimal. The hosts would want some stability in the second session and get a partnership going.

A dream session for Australia. Starc struck in his third over, then Hazlewood got one in the next before a procession began. Mathews and Chandimal tried to launch a counter-attack but both fell cheaply, with the latter getting dismissed 5 minutes before the break.
Full and on the pads, eased to backward square leg for a run. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Poor delivery, short and wide outside off, begging to be hit, Perera latches onto the opportunity to free his arms and slaps it through point for a boundary. He loves it there!
Fullish on off, driven to mid off.
FOUR! Uppish but safe! There is always a risk element involved with his batting. Short ball around leg, Perera goes on his toes and pulls it just wide of the mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
Fullish on off, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Anything short and being a back foot batsman de Silva will punish you on most occasions. Lyon serves a half-tracker outside off, de Silva rocks back and whacks it through point.
de Silva has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Too full in length and outside off, Perera drives it through the gap at covers for three runs.
Flighted ball on off, punched to covers.

NOT OUT! Good spot by the umpire, there is an inside edge. Flighted ball around off, from round the wicket to the left-hander, Perera gets half-forward in defense but fails to do so cleanly. They appeal vociferously but the umpire remains unmoved. Steven Smith opts for the review after consulting his players but the replays show an inside edge.
Australia have taken a review here. Nathan Lyon reckons that Kusal Perera might be out LBW. Umpire Richard Kettleborough has given him not out.
Tossed up ball on middle, flicked through square leg for a run.
Here is NATHAN LYON.
KUSAL PERERA walks in at number 7, replacing Chandimal. Sri Lanka would want to see off this 5-minute period before Lunch.

OUT! Gone! Beauty of a delivery and how important was the stop made by Warner in the previous ball? It's a team game after all. Hazlewood delivers a full ball just outside off, Chandimal with unsure footwork tries to play at it with a straight bat. The ball maybe moves away a shade due to which the outside edge is generated. Nevill dives to his right to take a very good catch. Sri Lanka now have their top five back in the hut!

DAVID WARNER, YOU BEAUTY! Saves a certain boundary and nearly affects a run out. Full in length and outside off, Chandimal plays a good looking drive off his front foot towards wide mid off. It races through and Warner reacts immediately to his left. He dives full length like a leopard and makes an outstanding stop. Quickly recovers from his dive and then has a shy at the non-striker's end. Misses and the debutant gets a life. Burns nicely backs up the throw and he scores a direct hit at the bowler's end but the batsman was safely in by then. Extraordinary piece of fielding.
Length ball outside off, Chandimal plays a mistimed drive towards mid off.
Down the leg side, on a length, Chandimal fails to flick and Nevill stops the ball nicely behind the stumps.
Bowls it full and on off, Chandimal plays a controlled off drive straight to the fielder.
Good length ball on middle, Chandimal tries to flick but misses as there is extra bounce. He is hit on the thigh pad.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Once again it's served on the slower side, 82 kph, maybe an arm ball, skidding in from middle, Chandimal gets it off the inside half of the bat through square leg for a single.
Slower through the air, full and dipping in around leg, 78 kph, Chandimal tries to sweep but fails to get any timing behind it.
Flighted on off, Chandimal goes back and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, pushed to covers.
Keeps it full and outside off, de Silva bunts it down to the off side.
This one is full and around off, de Silva looks to defend from the crease but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

FOUR! This boy is a very good back foot player and Australia should concentrate on bringing him forward (like they did to Root in 2013-14 Ashes). Hazlewood bangs in short on off, de Silva is on top of the bounce in a flash and pulls it aerially and over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full in length angling into the batsman, de Silva instead of getting forward, defends it from the crease to mid on.
Length on off, de Silva plays from the crease to the off side.
Good length ball on off, de Silva prefers to stay back in defense.
Lands it full and on off, Chandimal pushes it with the spin to short extra cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker one this time, around leg and skidding down, Chandimal fails to work it away and takes a hit on the pads.
Three in a row. O'Keefe sticks to the same line and length and DC has no issues in repeating the treatment.
Action replay of the previous ball.
Flighted ball on off, Chandimal gets on the front foot and pushes it to short extra cover.
On a length and outside off, holding its line, de Silva moves across a bit to cover the stumps and shoulders arms. Good leave!
Straighter in line, de Silva plays it down to square leg.
Short and pulled behind square leg for a single.
It has gone a touch overcast out there. Rain predictions were there for this game. Sri Lanka would not mind a break right now.
Good shot! Hazlewood drops his length full and outside off, Chandimal confidently gets on the front foot and drives it through covers for couple. Not timed that well!
A little bit of movement off the seam, coming into the batsman after landing, Chandimal defends it off the inside half of the bat.
Good length ball on off, Chandimal defends it from the back foot to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another watchful textbook front foot defensive shot.
Once again very full and around off, de Silva is forward with a straight bat in defense.
Too full in length on middle, de Silva defends it off his front foot to the off side.
Tossed up ball on off, defended with the spin to the off side.
On a length and wide outside off, too wide for the batsman to play.
Beauty of a delivery! Angling into the batsman, landing on a length around off, Chandimal tries to defend it by getting forward, but it shapes away a bit to beat the outside edge.
This time it's full and outside off, Chandimal is lured into the drive but he only manages to hit it straight to the point fielder, who is standing a bit deeper than the normal position.
Keeps his length and line straight, Chandimal covers the line and blocks it safely.
Fullish around off, Chandimal defends it off his front foot.
Good length ball on off, defended back to the bowler.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD is back into the attack.
Shorter and wider outside off, hit firmly to covers.
FOUR! This young man has impressed so far. O'Keefe drags his length short and lands it around middle, de Silva goes back on the back foot and smacks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Around off, defended from the crease by de Silva.
Flatter and shorter on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Full flighted on off, de Silva gets forward and pushes it to covers.
A bit short and around off, de Silva goes back and turns it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Hurls a length delivery in the zone outside off, Chandimal lets it through to end the over.
Width on offer outside off, Chandimal throws his bat at it and goes off the toe part of the bat at gully. Mitchell Marsh stationed there makes a half stop and parries it to third slip.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Good length ball on middle and off, de Silva defends it off his back foot. Looks like a solid back foot batsman.
Slightly short and around leg, Chandimal fails to work it on the leg side and it goes off his pads. The backward square leg fielder runs to his right to stop the ball and they cross for a leg bye.
Once again it's watchfully defended by de Silva.
Around off, de Silva has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Lunges and defends it down watchfully.

As expected, the bowler goes short with his length after going for a biggie, quicker and flatter as well, 89 kph, de Silva is immediately on the back foot, nice anticipation and punches it through cover-point for a couple of runs. Looks like a promising lad!

SIX! Ho! Ho! Ho! That's some way of getting off the mark on debut! de Silva shows no nerves, runs down the track in a jiffy, reaches the ball in a flash and launches it over the bowler's head. Boom, away she goes and sails over the ropes. It seems he is a naturally aggressive batsman.
Once again a back foot defense by Chandimal to end the over.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Digs in a short ball to push the batsman back, Chandimal sits under it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Back of a length ball around leg, Chandimal tries to flick but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
Skidding down, Silva fails to flick and is hit on the thigh pad.
Once again it's defended by the batsman by coming forward.
Flatter on off, defended off the back foot.
Gets on the front foot and defends it watchfully.
Dhananjaya de Silva walks in next. Big pressure on the debutant!

OUT! Mathews is done and dusted! Extra bounce does the trick and Sri Lanka are in deep, deep trouble. A tossed up ball on off, good line, luring the batsman forward, Mathews presses on his front foot, tries to defend but the ball spins away with extra lift to catch the shoulder of the bat. The Australian skipper Steven Smith grabs a fine low catch at first slip. He does not miss many!
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot to point. With the spin!
Bumper! Starc digs it in short, Chandimal ducks underneath it.
Slants across a full ball outside off, Chandimal drives it square of the wicket on the off side for a couple of runs.
On a length around middle, defended off the pads to mid-wicket.

FOUR! Nicely played shot again and a good effort by Warner goes in vain. Starc pitches it full and Chandimal executes a lovely drive straight down the ground. Warner goes after it from mid off, tries to pull it back with a forward dive near the fence but fails to do the job.
Good length ball angling away from the batsman, Chandimal covers the line and shoulders arms.
FOUR! Starc goes for a yorker but ends up slipping a low full toss on middle, Chandimal does well to pick it up and whip it through square leg for a boundary.
Once again the length is on the shorter side, Mathews goes back and nicely punches it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Oohhh...that missed the off stump by a whisker. A touch shortish on off, skidding through, Mathews tries to cut but misses.
Another watchful front foot defense by Angelo.
Drops it full again, around off, Mathews gets on the front foot and defends.
Just a touch short in length on off, Mathews punches it from the crease to covers.
Flighted full ball around off, Mathews lunges in defense.

DRINKS are on the field. A poor over rate by Australia but that is because they have picked up 3 wickets. Not surprisingly, it is down to the two most experienced pair in the middle. Australia will be searching for that one wicket and then hope to run through the rest.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Short and outside off, a poor ball, 136 kph, Mathews cuts it through point for a boundary.
Again, Angelo tucks it towards Khawaja and he dives to stop it once more.
On middle, a predictable short ball, 139 kph, Mathews hops and works it behind square leg. There is a man stationed at short fine leg, Usman Khawaja, who dives but the lands just short.
A bouncer now, Mathews ducks.

EDGED! DOES NOT CARRY! Starc almost gets his man first ball! Full and around off, 143 kph, swinging away, Mathews is squared up and the ball goes behind, dropping short of Nevill who dives to his right. The slip cordon has its hands on its head, feeling that it is an edge which did not carry. Starc though, appeals for LBW. Replays show that it took the outside edge.
Okay then. The bowler who said he will target Mathews is back into the attack. MITCHELL STARC vs ANGELO MATHEWS - Round 1.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and just outside off, 84 kph, defended watchfully.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, 85 kph, watchfully defended.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
FOUR! Uppish, but safe! Full and outside off, 77 kph, Mathews drives this loosely, in the air, but evades the man at covers and gets a boundary.
Full and outside off, 136 kph, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, punched through point for a couple.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Full and outside off, 139 kph, driven towards mid on.

A huge cheer goes around the ground. CAPTAIN ANGELO MATHEWS walks out at number 5, replacing Silva. A big moment in the match. Before the game, Mitchell Starc said that he will target him. Peter Nevill shouts behind the stumps, "HERE WE GO, BOYS! HERE WE GO! "

OUT! Edged and taken! McGrathesque line. Full and just outside off, 138 kph. You have got to play at that. Else you will be knocked over. Silva realizes that. He pushes forward. Looks to defend. However, that is the trick of that line. It deviates ever so slightly, takes the outside edge and goes low to Adam Voges at first slip who cups it beautifully. Hard luck for Silva. Cannot do much with those. Play them, you edge and go back to the pavillion. Leave them alone, you still go back to the pavillion, LBW or bowled. Australia on top at the moment.
Full and outside off, 85 kph, driven back to the bowler.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Outside off, 84 kph, well defended.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Full and outside off, 80 kph, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, 77 kph, watchfully defended.
Okay. We have the first change. And it is not Mitchell Marsh. It is the hero of the warm-up game - STEPHEN O'KEEFE.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
A short ball outside off, 136 kph, Chandimal sways away.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, 143 kph, left alone.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Stays back in his crease and blocks it out.
On middle and leg, worked through square leg for a single.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, pushed straight to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
DINESH CHANDIMAL walks in at number 4, replacing Mendis.

OUT! LBW! The second one is down! A full ball outside off, 137 kph, Mendis plays all over it, looking to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Hazlewood appeals and the umpire raises his finger! Mendis has a word with his partner, thinks about the review and then takes it. However, he has taken too long and has been TIMED OUT! You are allowed 15 seconds to inform the umpire that you want to take the review and Mendis took longer than that. Anyways replays show that he is dead plumb.
Outside off, 138 kph, pushed straight back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, 146 kph, a play and a miss from Mendis.

MISFIELD! FOUR! What a shot. Full and down the leg side, 143 kph, Mendis flicks it uppishly behind square leg. There is Josh Hazlewood at the boundary but he gets a bad bounce and the ball goes through! Captain Steven Smith shows his first signs of anger.
FOUR! Short and outside off, 144 kph, cut behind point for a boundary.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
KUSAL MENDIS walks in at number 3, replacing Karunaratne.

OUT! LBW! The decision stays as it is! A good length ball angling in, 137 kph, Karunaratne looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. He is given out and he takes the review. It takes a while for the Hawk Eye to work and eventually, it shows that the ball is hitting leg stump. First strike by Australia.
Karunaratne has been adjudged LBW! He has taken the first review of this match.
This one jags back in, hits Silva on the pads as he looks to flick. Going down leg.
On a good length outside off, 141 kph, Kaushal pushes inside the line and gets a thick outside edge which lands short of second slip.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Outside off, 137 kph, not played at.
LEADING EDGE! SAFE! On a good length around off, Silva looks to work it to the leg side but gets a leading edge which lands wide of the bowler.
Full and outside off, 135 kph, left alone.
A bouncer now, 140 kph, Dimuth ducks.
Full and outside off, 144 kph, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A bouncer on middle, 145 kph, Dimuth ducks.
This one swings back in, Karunaratne looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.

Full and on middle, swinging in, 142 kph, Karunaratne looks to defend but the bat turns in his hand and the ball goes past mid on. David Warner gives it a chase and the batsmen come back for the second.
Full and outside off, 141 kph, well defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Pushes it towards mid on.
Full and outside off, 133 kph, not played at.
Outside off, 138 kph, left alone.
Full on middle and leg, 137 kph, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD to share the new ball with Starc.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
The batsman has played it to the point region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
There comes an inswinging yorker at 145 kph, outside off, Karunaratne looks to dig it out but the ball goes off the inside edge past the stumps to fine leg. A single taken.
Full on middle, played to short mid-wicket.

Okay. The national anthems are done and dusted and the Australians get into a huddle. Out come the Sri Lankan openers - DIMUTH KARUNARATNE AND KAUSHAL SILVA. MITCHELL STARC to start off proceedings. Karunaratne to face. Here we go...
The teams are lining up for the national anthems - Australia first, followed by the Sri Lankan one.

STEVEN SMITH says that it looks a very dry wicket. Smiles on learning that Sri Lanka are playing four spinners as opposed to his side's 2. Confirms that David Warner is fit and hopes he scores big in this game. Admits that it is very hot out there and he is already perspiring.

ANGELO MATHEWS says that the wicket looks very good but it might take some turn on Day 2. Informs that Dhananjaya de Silva and the chinaman, Lakshan Sanadakan are making their Test debut. Is confident of a good show from his side as there are plenty of players to watch out for.
TOSS - Mathews spins the call, heads is the call, it is a tail. SRI LANKA CHOOSE TO BAT.

PITCH REPORT - Russell Arnold doing the pitch report says that traditionally the Pallekele pitch is a good one to bat upon. He feels spinners will have a say later on in the match. Opines that it is a bat first pitch.
WEATHER REPORT - There was rain forecast for most of the days in this game but right now, there is bright sunshine.

No Ponting. No Hussey. No Warne. No Murali. No Vaas. No Mahela. But still, there is plenty of excitement as Australia gets ready to tour Sri Lanka for one more time - a 3-Test series, followed by a 5-ODI and a lone T20I. Strangely, in spite of a poor Asian record, Australia have done decently in the Island nation. What will we see this time around? Hello and a warm welcome to the opening Test between Sri Lanka and Australia at Pallekele.
